ow-tp-portal-<ns>-feedback-projection (Lambda java17, SQS event source mapping, batch 5, ReportBatchItemFailures)
ow-tp-portal-<ns>-feedback-stats (DynamoDB, PAY_PER_REQUEST, PITR; stats item + evt#/triage# idempotency markers)
ow-tp-portal-<ns>-feedback-triage (Step Functions Standard state machine: validate -> record triage -> quarantine on failure)
ow-tp-portal-<ns>-feedback-events-dlq-depth / -feedback-projection-errors / -feedback-events-age (CloudWatch alarms, wired into the alarm->Devin rule)
golden_baseline_location: scripts/tp_portal/golden/portal-golden-transcript.json (unchanged: the async path is additive; every one of the 20 steps keeps its exact status and body)

acceptance_checks.description: POST /api/feedback keeps write-then-publish semantics: the 201 body reflects the committed DynamoDB write exactly as today (golden transcript step passes unchanged). The FeedbackSubmitted event is published to the custom bus only after the write commits; a publish failure is logged and never fails the committed request — the events-published==submissions recon check is the detector for a silent publish gap. The async result becomes visible through the existing GET /api/feedback/average-rating route's value being reproduced by the projection (new derived read model), not by changing any golden response.
Events published equals feedback submissions accepted (201) during the window, recomputed from the target (projection dedupe markers + queue counters), never from producer memory.

The feedback-stats projection (count, ratingSum) converges to exactly the value the synchronous GET /api/feedback/average-rating computes from the feedback table; equality of the two averages is the parity check.
Main queue depth 0 and DLQ depth 0 on the green path after processing; consumer errors 0.

Replaying an already-processed event (same deterministic event id) is a provable no-op: dedupe marker evt#<eventId> conditional put fails, stats unchanged. Proven by an actual rerun/redelivery, not inferred.

Red path: N poison messages exhaust maxReceiveCount=3 and land in the DLQ with full payload; DLQ depth == N (set comparison, missing and unexpected); after the operator fix + scripts/tp_portal/replay_dlq.py redrive, DLQ depth 0 and the projection converged again; other contexts unaffected.

The feedback-triage Standard state machine records one triage marker per event with an explicit Retry (backoff on States.TaskFailed) and Catch -> Quarantine (SQS SendMessage to the DLQ); green path executions succeed with zero failures, red path shows a visible retry in execution history.
Producer role adds only events:PutEvents on the custom bus; consumer role reads exactly one queue and writes exactly one table; queue policy and workflow role carry source-ARN conditions.

planted_anomalies.description: Retryable-class failure exhausted: with the projection store broken (missing stats table), a valid event fails 3 receives and must be captured in the DLQ with full payload; after the operator restores the store and runs replay_dlq.py the message must process and the projection converge.

Non-retryable schema violation (malformed JSON detail / missing eventId / rating outside 1-5) must be classified poison by the consumer (batch item failure every receive) and reach the DLQ; proven by consumer unit tests in fixture runs.
DLQ-depth alarm OK->ALARM->OK and alarm->Devin webhook delivery on the live estate; live-only, owned by the parent's validation window.
planted_anomalies.reason: Child runs are fixture-only (LocalStack); CloudWatch alarm state transitions cannot be exercised there.

encoding_policy.input_encoding: UTF-8 JSON throughout: the EventBridge event detail is the UTF-8 JSON FeedbackSubmitted payload; SQS delivers the full EventBridge envelope as a UTF-8 JSON body. Payloads are a few hundred bytes, far under the 256KB EventBridge/SQS limit (message field capped at 2000 chars by the synchronous contract).
encoding_policy.byte_transparency: Not byte-transparent: events are compared as parsed JSON values; the deterministic eventId (UUIDv5 over 'feedback:<feedbackId>') is the identity, not the serialized bytes.
encoding_policy.invalid_bytes: A body that does not decode as UTF-8 JSON is a non-retryable poison message: classified as a batch item failure on every receive until redrive delivers it to the DLQ intact.

malformed_record_policy.details: Unknown JSON fields in the event detail are ignored (non-strict binding). Non-retryable poison = malformed JSON, missing/empty eventId, feedbackId, or userId, rating outside 1-5, oversized detail. Retryable = DynamoDB throttle/transient SDK failure. Both classes surface as SQS batch item failures; retryables usually succeed within maxReceiveCount=3, poisons exhaust it and land in the DLQ with full payload. NULLs never fail open into the projection.

empty_input_semantics.details: An idle estate is silent: no submissions means no events, no executions, no phantom consumer invocations, and no alarms (treat_missing_data=notBreaching on every async alarm). An SQS delivery with zero parseable records returns an empty batch response. The projection over an empty window reports averageRating 0.0, matching the synchronous route.

trigger_granularity_note: SQS event source mapping with batch_size=5, no batching window (portal-scale volume), function_response_types=ReportBatchItemFailures: a partial batch failure retries only the failed messages, and idempotent consumption makes any redelivery of a succeeded message a no-op. Queue visibility timeout (10s) >= consumer timeout (10s) so the platform accepts the mapping and a poison message reaches the DLQ within a demo beat (~30s). The triage workflow is per-event (one execution per FeedbackSubmitted). No SnapStart on the consumer (event-source-mapping-driven; the pending-optimization window would fake code faults).
